text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croat-Moslem Federation's parliament appointed a new government in Sarajevo on Wednesday. Federal Prime Minister will be Edhem Bicakcic, a Moslem, while his deputy and finance minister, Drago Bilandzija, a Croat.

- German car manufacturer "Opel" will open its sales showroom in collaboration with Bosnian holding company "Bosna Auto" in Sarajevo on Thursday. Opel export discount of 33 per cent for Bosnia will mean that cars will be cheaper in Sarajevo than in Germany.
- Another Moslem family was ousted from Croat-held part of Mostar on Tuesday, Mostar police reports.

- Stolac talks which were supposed to appoint an interim town council composed of Croat and Moslem representatives failed despite proposal made by international mediator for the federation Christian Schwartz-Shilling.
